app: Splunk Edge Hub (Modbus TCP client), Splunk OT Intelligence
spl:
index=edge_hub_modbus
| lookup modbus_register_map deviceName startingAddress OUTPUT register_name
| search register_name IN ("voltage", "current", "frequency")
| stats latest(value) as latest_val by register_name, deviceName, captureHostname
| eval latest_val=tonumber(latest_val)
| eval register_healthy=case(
    register_name="voltage" AND latest_val >= 210 AND latest_val <= 250, "YES",
    register_name="current" AND latest_val >= 0 AND latest_val <= 100, "YES",
    register_name="frequency" AND latest_val >= 49 AND latest_val <= 51, "YES",
    1=1, "NO")
| where register_healthy="NO"

value: For 'Modbus TCP Register Monitoring for Industrial Equipment', UC-14.3.32 converts `activity` on `_json` feeds into actionable rows and reduces operational risk and delayed incident response.
implementation: Configure Modbus TCP in Advanced Settings → Modbus tab with equipment IP/port (default 502). Define register map (coils, discrete inputs, holding registers, input registers) with OID aliases for readability. Configure polling interval (10-30 seconds typical) and register read strategy (optimized batching). Store register values in edge_hub_modbus (events) or as metrics in edge_hub_data. Map register indices to human-readable tags (e.g., 0x1234→"VFD_Speed_Hz"). Local SQLite backlog stores 100K Modbus events for offline resilience. Edge Hub Modbus events identify a register by deviceName and startingAddress, so keep a `modbus_register_map` lookup that names each register (voltage, current, frequency) from the meter's register map.
visualization: Register value trend, equipment health gauge, Modbus gateway connection status.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable (no CIM or Operational_Telemetry data model in this SPL).

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Edge Hub (Modbus TCP client), Splunk OT Intelligence.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=edge_hub_modbus` (Modbus register reads: hub_name, captureHostname, deviceName, startingAddress, endingAddress, unitIdentifier, value, functionCode); `modbus_register_map` lookup (deviceName, startingAddress, register_name) from the equipment register map. Sent to HEC by a Splunk Edge Hub OS Datastreamer configured in Splunk OT Intelligence (Edge Hub OS does not support a universal forwarder).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure Modbus TCP in Advanced Settings → Modbus tab with equipment IP/port (default 502). Define register map (coils, discrete inputs, holding registers, input registers) with OID aliases for readability. Configure polling interval (10-30 seconds typical) and register read strategy (optimized batching). Store register values in edge_hub_modbus (events) or as metrics in edge_hub_data. Map register indices to human-readable tags (e.g., 0x1234→"VFD_Speed_Hz"). Local SQLite backlog stores 100K Modb…

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=edge_hub_modbus
| lookup modbus_register_map deviceName startingAddress OUTPUT register_name
| search register_name IN ("voltage", "current", "frequency")
| stats latest(value) as latest_val by register_name, deviceName, captureHostname
| eval latest_val=tonumber(latest_val)
| eval register_healthy=case(
    register_name="voltage" AND latest_val >= 210 AND latest_val <= 250, "YES",
    register_name="current" AND latest_val >= 0 AND latest_val <= 100, "YES",
    register_name="frequency" AND latest_val >= 49 AND latest_val <= 51, "YES",
    1=1, "NO")
| where register_healthy="NO"
```

Understanding this SPL

**Modbus TCP Register Monitoring for Industrial Equipment** — Monitors equipment operational parameters via Modbus registers without requiring specialized data collection agents.

Documented **Data sources**: `index=edge_hub_modbus` (Modbus register reads: hub_name, captureHostname, deviceName, startingAddress, endingAddress, unitIdentifier, value, functionCode); `modbus_register_map` lookup (deviceName, startingAddress, register_name) from the equipment register map. Sent to HEC by a Splunk Edge Hub OS Datastreamer configured in Splunk OT Intelligence (Edge Hub OS does not support a universal forwarder). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Edge Hub (Modbus TCP client), Splunk OT Intelligence. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: edge_hub_modbus.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=edge_hub_modbus. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• Enriches events using `lookup` (lookup definition + optional OUTPUT fields).
• Applies an explicit `search` filter to narrow the current result set.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by register_name, deviceName, captureHostname** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions (useful for per-host, per-user, or per-entity comparisons for this use case).
• `eval` defines or adjusts **latest_val** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **register_healthy** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where register_healthy="NO"` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

Step 3 — Validate
Confirm metric or event volume in the time range, then compare trends and device status to the Splunk Edge Hub admin UI or the mobile app for the same devices. Verify metric names, hosts, and time skew.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Register value trend, equipment health gauge, Modbus gateway connection status.

productArtifacts.title: Datastreamer for Modbus data
productArtifacts.body:
Add the Modbus TCP server and the register ranges to read on the hub (Splunk Edge Hub OS: Configure Splunk Edge Hub OS to communicate with electronic devices using the Modbus protocol).

In Splunk OT Intelligence, open Data Ingestion and create a Datastreamer:
HEC hostname: the HTTP Event Collector URL of your Splunk platform deployment
HEC token: a token whose allowed indexes include the index below
Name: modbus
Index: edge_hub_modbus (events index)
Topics: edgehub/modbus
Source Type: _json
